reasoning: As of March 2026, polling shows Tisza leading by 8-12 points among decided voters, but Hungary's electoral system heavily favors larger parties through single-member constituencies. Fidesz has historically outperformed polls and controls significant state resources. The opposition needs a 3-5 point national vote lead just to win a majority due to gerrymandering. Pro-government pollsters show Fidesz ahead, and many voters remain undecided. Given Fidesz's structural advantages, incumbency benefits, and historical resilience, despite trailing in independent polls, I estimate roughly even odds with slight edge to Fidesz.
